title: O people of the world, keep watching!
lead: A song in Hindi/Urdu dedicated to Neohumanism. It shows how spiritual humanism through love unites loving hearts with the Supreme Principle forever.

words.meaning_here: O inhabitants of this fleeting world

words.role: auxiliary verb as part of continuous aspect

words.meaning_here: continue to remain (tākte raho: keep watching / do not look away)

lines.structure: Address (DUNIYÁVÁLOṊ) + compound continuous verbal predicate in imperative mood (TÁKTE RAHO).
lines.literal: O people of the world, gazing intently continue to remain!
lines.natural: O people of the world, behold and keep watching!
lines.image_note: The song is composed in Hindi/Urdu. An address to people immersed in worldly affairs, calling upon them to witness the unfolding spiritual transformation.

words.etymology: Sanskrit aham -> Shauraseni Prakrit hamme -> Hindi ham

words.form: plural, oblique case with dative/accusative marker -ko
words.meaning_here: to the sights, to the seeking gazes (of those looking towards Him)
an offering, a precious present (of Myself)
words.etymology: Arabic/Persian nazrāna (gift presented in reverence or love)

words.form: past perfect tense from jānā (to go), plural
words.role: auxiliary verb in a compound action
words.meaning_here: departed, continued doing (diye gaye: gave unsparingly)
words.etymology: Sanskrit gata -> Prakrit gaa -> Hindi gayā

lines.structure: Subject (HAM) + indirect object (NAZAROṊKO) + direct object (NAZARÁNÁ) + compound predicate of completed process (DIYE GYAYE).
lines.literal: We [to seeking] gazes a gift granted and went on.
lines.natural: To every seeking gaze, I bestowed a precious gift.
lines.image_note: A wordplay on the root 'nazar' (glance, sight) and 'nazrāna' (a gift offered at a meeting). To the devotee's seeking gaze, the Lord offers Himself.

words.form: stem of verb phailnā (to spread, diffuse)

lines.structure: Modifier (INSÁNIYAT KII) + modifier (IYAH) + subject (ROSHNII) + compound predicate (PHAEL GAYII).
lines.literal: Of humanism this light has spread.
lines.natural: Now this light of true humanism has spread everywhere,
lines.image_note: The light of Neohumanism dispels the darkness of dogmas and narrowness, illuminating the entire world.

words.etymology: Arabic rūḥ (spirit, soul) + relative adjective suffix -ānī

words.meaning_here: in the heart, inside the mind

words.etymology: Sanskrit madhya (middle) -> Prakrit majjhe -> Hindi meṋ

words.form: past perfect tense, feminine (agrees with insániyat)

lines.structure: Modifier (RÚHÁNII) + subject (INSÁNIYAT) + adverbial of place (DIL ME) + predicate (ÁYII).
lines.literal: Spiritual humanity into the heart has entered.
lines.natural: Spiritual humanism has entered into every heart.
lines.image_note: Neohumanism is humanism rooted in the spiritual bond connecting all living beings with the One Creator.

words.meaning_here: those endowed with a loving heart; generous, devoted souls
words.etymology: Persian dil (heart) + dār (holding) + Hindi agentive marker ne

words.meaning_here: what indeed, what an incredible wonder
words.etymology: Sanskrit kim -> Prakrit kia -> Hindi kyā

words.form: past perfect tense, masculine (agrees with yah/kyā)
words.etymology: Sanskrit kṛta -> Prakrit kia -> Hindi kiyā

lines.structure: Subject in ergative case (DIL DÁRON NE) + object (IYAH) + question word (KYÁ) + predicate (KIYÁ).
lines.literal: By those with heart this what was done?
lines.natural: And what have these loving hearts done?
lines.image_note: A rhetorical question of wonder: through love, devotees have achieved the miracle of union with the Infinite.

words.form: 1st person plural used as majestic singular
plural, oblique case with possessive postposition -ke
words.meaning_here: of all people, of every creature
to their hearts, with their souls
inseparably adhered, firmly bonded, inextricably merged
words.etymology: Persian chaspidan (to stick, cling, unite closely)

words.form: auxiliary verb of completion (from jānā), plural

lines.structure: Subject (HAM) + intensifier (TO) + modifier (SABOṊKE) + object (DILOṊSE) + compound predicative predicate (CASAP GYAYE).
lines.literal: I indeed to all's hearts inextricably clinging have become.
lines.natural: For I have become inextricably bound to the hearts of all.
lines.image_note: The word 'chasp' conveys total inseparability, where the Divine has clinged inextricably to the loving hearts of the devotees.

interpretation: The song is written in Hindi/Urdu and heralds the dawn of the Neohumanist era. The Lord calls out to the entire world: to those who genuinely sought the ultimate truth, He revealed Himself. Spiritual humanism is not merely an abstract philosophy, but a light transforming the human heart. Those who cultivate unconditional love have bound the Lord in bonds of devotion so firmly that He has become inseparable from their hearts.
